meta.title: `remove-unnecessary-else` bad suggestions and false positives on thread_local macro
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#16590 (fix: Fix false positives for "unnecessary else" diagnostic)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2024-02-19 and 2024-02-26; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2024-02-26. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1).
meta.notes: The new remove-unnecessary-else diagnostic fired when the then-branch diverges (return) even if the if is an expression whose value is used (a let initializer with else-if); its fix then splits the let's if-else chain into a statement and a second if, which does not parse. The fix restricts the diagnostic to if statements. The thread_local! false positive of the same issue needs the reporter's projects (no minimal reproduction) and is not part of the case.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.source: issue body, first code block ('Bad suggestions: Given this code')

files.note: a binary crate around the snippet (package name, version, edition 2021)

repro.steps: Open src/main.rs. The diagnostic remove-unnecessary-else (weak warning) is reported on the else of 'let query = if files.is_empty() { return; } else if ...'. Apply its fix 'Remove unnecessary else block'. Reported: the let initializer is cut after the first if ('let query = if files.is_empty() { return; }' followed by a separate 'if files.len() == 1 {...}'), which doesn't compile. Probe: the edited text must have no parse error that the original did not have; no fix offered means absent (the fix stops reporting the diagnostic here).
